title: Subtle manipulation in our culture
description: Everyone partakes in manipulation. Our culture really disconnects us from ourselves. We all get too much in our heads with our fear and ego. The social situations of the holiday season can make things worse.
videoTitle: NFTH Talks with Tom Campbell-Letting the Holidays Happen!

description: Working from home is better for people's lives in many ways. Most people who were able to work from home prefer it to working in-person in an office environment.
videoTitle: NFTH Talks with Tom Campbell-Letting the Holidays Happen!

title: Let the holidays happen and be authentic
description: Let the holidays happen, enjoy them and be a part of them! No expectations. Socialization is where we learn - where the rubber meets the road. Deal with things positively and you will have fun.
videoTitle: NFTH Talks with Tom Campbell-Letting the Holidays Happen!

title: A Short Introduction to My Big TOE

title: A different approach to letting go of fears
description: Tom gives a better way to think about uncovering fear, how to assess if we are getting rid of it, and potential pitfalls and ego traps to be aware of
videoTitle: FEARS: Advice from Tom Campbell on Better Ways to Uncover Them

title: Is it easier to hang on to our fears? And is every negative emotion indicative of a fear?
description: Getting rid of fear is generally uncomfotable and we're really good at finding justification for our fears. We have to let go of wanting things to be exactly as we want them to be. Acceptance and dealing with things positively is the best course.
videoTitle: FEARS: Advice from Tom Campbell on Better Ways to Uncover Them

title: How to get the message out to let others know that the best way to change the world is to change ourselves
description: People don't want to hear that they're doing things wrong. Ego and belief make the fear invisible and skew perspective. Be helpful, but separate whats truly being helpful vs what you really want yourself. Stop trying to fix other people - instead, be mindful and find a solution.
videoTitle: FEARS: Advice from Tom Campbell on Better Ways to Uncover Them

title: Awareness of fear and dealing with it positively
description: Be careful that you don't turn your fear into an ego or belief that makes you want to go out and fix other people. Manipulation is not the way. Be mindful of others and act with empathy. There is no one size fits all, every situation is different, lowering entropy is the goal.
videoTitle: FEARS: Advice from Tom Campbell on Better Ways to Uncover Them

title: Primal women and men in early civilization
description: Back in primal civilization, women had to deal with their partners dying off. Our species split the jobs that kept us from dying off. Primal woman was more risk averse than primal man.
videoTitle: Front Row Seat Interviews Tom Campbell: Primal Man Primal Woman 2 of 2

title: Instincts and modern society. The differences between men and women
description: Our primal environment in which our instincts developed was one in which survival was very hard. Our modern environment is dramatically different. Women are in-tune with the inside world of relationships while men are in-tune with the outside world.
videoTitle: Front Row Seat Interviews Tom Campbell: Primal Man Primal Woman 2 of 2

title: Male/female emotional instincts
description: Men are intuitive in the relationship world rather than intellectual and women are the opposite. Repressing insticts is not good. Deal with them positively and make the best low entropy choices you can.
videoTitle: Front Row Seat Interviews Tom Campbell: Primal Man Primal Woman 2 of 2

description: Characteristics and traits for survivability in primal male/female. Understanding and awareness about why these instincts still persist.
videoTitle: Front Row Seat Interviews Tom Campbell: Primal Man Primal Woman 2 of 2

videoTitle: Front Row Seat Interviews Tom Campbell: Primal Man Primal Woman 2 of 2

title: The experience of dissociation
description: There is always choice involved when entering a dissociative state. Some experiences of dissociation are choosing to stay in observation mode. We can be overwhelmed and not aware of any other choice aside from listening and watching. Decision space encompasses only the choices you are aware of, and not the entirety of choices available to you.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: Decision fatigue - are there too many choices, and can we simplify them?
description: You always have a choice as to how many choices you want to make. You can simplify as you see fit. Things that matter to you, and your degree of comfort will influence how engaged you want to be. You can always prioritize to avoid a frenzied state. Downtime is important.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: How can we balance ourselves and optimize our growth?
description: Many people stay with doing what's easiest and most natural and avoid the things that are more challenging. It's important to challenge ourselves. Having more than one persona is one way of balancing things e.g. work persona and personal life persona. All of these personas are all part of you.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: How much of our personality can we actually change if some way of being isn't working out?
description: You don't have to change who you are. Be yourself, but it's the approach and the attitude that needs to change in order to fit the situation. There are times we need to do things that we don't like.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: How does consciousness influence healing? What are the differences between healing ourselves and healing someone else?
description: Modifying future probability of the possibilities, with our intent, is how we heal others and ourselves. Focus, specificity, and disciplining our mind and mental energy will make us more effective. Uncertainty in probability also influences the outcome.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: How effective is modifying future probability towards a negative or selfish outcome?
description: The LCS doesn’t want to work against itself. It has an interest in evolving and lower entropy, not raising it. If you have negative intent for personal gain you're not going to be very successful in the long run.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: Quality of consciousness and different cultures. Is evil winning in Western culture?
description: Culture is a broad, collective consciousness and most are a mixed bag. IUOCs are incarnating to grow up, and we grow up by rising to challenges and making good decisions. Western culture is not particularly very evil, but has some parts of it that are negative. There are also good things and a lot of change, choices, and opportunity for growth.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: Negative values and organized global destruction
description: Our PMR is a kindergarten. We have a lot of fear, and that's why there's a lot of negativity in the world. As humans, we operate in management by crisis. This is the level of awareness in the average human who is largely self-centered. Those that have the most control, power, and force are going to try and maintain that. However, this is temporary. We learn by mistake, slowly but surely, and negativity self-destructs eventually. The only thing stable is love.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 1/2

title: Tom's experience in another PMR
description: Tom talks about another PMR he visited that was much more negative than our own. It took less than a generation for that PMR to start to get more posisitve. Love always wins in the bigger picture.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: MBT and the concept of faith
description: Faith is a belief. If you are not a very grown up person, faith and belief will play a bigger part of your life. Low entropy will help you gain acceptance for things with uncertainty.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Helping people with anxiety
description: If someone is having an anxiety attack, it’s a fear attack that is immobilizing. There is no intellectual solution. Analyzing, giving solutions, and explaining their anxiety away will not help. Sit with them, be with them, comfort them. When the attack is gone, you may be able to help them discover the basic fear.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Tips on coping with and counteracting anxiety
description: If someone has anxiety, its often a negative self-referential issue. The more they can connect with other people, the better they will feel. Anxiety is a self-created monster and a negative attitude towards oneself. Sleep can help reboot the nervous system. Meditation can help too, but will take longer to get to the point where it can be a useful tool during an anxiety attack.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Anxiety while thinking about the LCS. Thinking oneself into anxiety when coming into bigger picture understanding
description: There is no certain answer to what is outside the system, but there is some speculation. One is spontaneous actualization of potential aka emergent complexity theroy, and the other is cellular autometa.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Dysfunctional beliefs and fears from childhood
description: If your fears and beliefs from childhood are causing trouble in your life, have the courage to try and be some other way. Give those fears the space they need to change. Be skeptical, even with yourself.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Is social media a sign of progress or regress?
description: Social media is both a sign of progress and regress. The ability to communicate and access information gives new opportunities. A lot of the problems we have socially are because of the internet, so we have to learn from and deal with the negatives.
videoTitle: The 87th Fireside Chat with Thomas W. Campbell December 2022 Pt. 2/2

title: Decision space and free will choices
description: Our decision space are all the free will choices available to us. It is the space in which we can decide which choice to make. As we lower our entropy, our decision space grows. As our intuition grows our awareness expands.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: Nested Virtual Realities
description: The concept of nested virtual realities. Each layer is dependent on the one above it. Too many layers would be inefficient, but one or two would make more sense. Consciousness is part of a process fractal.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: Consciousness Evolution and Biological Evolution
description: Tom discusses the differences between consciousness evolution and biological evolution. Although each is independently evolving, the LCS most likely tweaks the virtual reality from time to time to optimize its functionality in order to make it more effective as an entropy reduction tool.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: How to deal with potential negativity in conscious computers
description: We will be able to deal with any negative situations that come up as conscious computers evolve. Hollywood's portrayal of conscious computers is negative and scary because it sells. We'll have many checks and balances to create a productive environment with regard to conscious computers.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: Being Level vs Intellect
description: The being level is who you are at your core. Our intellectual level is the level at which we typically interact - its all about doing (e.g.judging, analyzing, comparing). We have fear in our being level, but our intellect makes a lot of choices based on that fear. Our intuition is also at our being level.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: Expert Systems, Algorithms vs Awareness
description: An expert system could act like its conscious if you can program into it every possible potential response to every possible potential conversation. This is highly impractical, so you would eventually find out that the expert system is not conscious. Algorithms are not awareness. A conscious computer would vary in its consistency. It may even get confused, or give you different answers when asked the same question more than once.
videoTitle: Viktor Erdelyi and Tom Campbell Discuss Conscious Computers

title: How time works in a simulation
description: Each simulation has an outer time loop. Planck time is the highest resolution of our simulation. The calculation is done one thing at a time, but its all done and updated within one delta t. You can never be more than a delta t different (10 to the -44 seconds) which is beyond our capability to measure.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Communicating with deceased relatives
description: Tom explains that no one typically gets stuck after death. We all have to learn our own lessons, and sometimes there are things we need to learn after death from our past incarnation.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Anti-Rats and Negative beings
description: Anti-rats are beings that are devolving. They can get to where they seem powerful by practicing negatively, but they can only grow so much due to the fear and ego that limits them. In the bigger picture, they're not really all that powerful to beings that are evolving positively. Positivity has no limit.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Love in a science framework
description: Love is rational, it's about other. Fear is irrational. The nature of our consciousness system is love. As we grow towards love and lowering entropy, we grow towards optimizing this system for everybody. Love wins, everybody wins.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Where and when are the probability distributions calculated
description: Probability distributions are calculated every Delta T. Within our decision space are probable possibilities assessed on our past.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: A probabilistic vs deterministic simulation
description: For everything thats unknown, the LCS has to do a probability draw. However, most things that are unknown to us, are known to the LCS, so it is not guessing as much as we are. Sometimes the LCS can manipulate uncertainty without any notice. Using probability distributions is simple, effective, offers easier calculations.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: How does the LCS make random draws of probability?
description: Whether or not it's a truly random draw is no relevant. There are event-based number generators being modeled by the LCS. There can be a really good computed number generator as long as there is no noticeable bias or repetitions in it.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: The second law of thermodynamics
description: The second law of thermodynamics is so fundamental that it can be considered cosmic law. It brings stability and usefulness to the system. Without it, reality would be deterministic.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Entropy in consciousness space
description: There has to be some way that order can be increased as a function of experience. This is how growth happens. Constant evolution requires constant effort.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Evolving to Love is a real thing
description: The LCS realized it had to break itself into independent pieces with free will in order to grow. Creating IUOCs raised the potential of the LCS. Cooperation makes it happen. Optimized social arrangements lower entropy.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Notes on meditation practices
description: If you are creating fears in meditation practice, you are not quite ready for those practices yet. Sometimes people can get into situations that are over their head and things become negative. Let these fear creating practices go and come back to it after you've grown.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Is our system both benevolent and malevolent?
description: It's not necessary for the LCS to be both benevolent and malevolent. The possibilities are both there, but the system had to grow up, and poor choices didn't take it very far. The system is not as fearful as we are. It had some arrogance in its younger days, but it is now extremely low entropy, and is very loving. If you are seeing malevolence, you need to ask if you are seeing something else.
videoTitle: Tom Campbell Answers Your Questions New Year's Edition 2023

title: Visiting other realities and the concept of identity
description: Most people don't experience a body when visiting other realities. You don't travel with your avatar. When you go out of body, you are just mind. If you are interacting with other beings, then you have a body, but you only see what you create there. You are getting a single player datastream to interpret.

Whether the light was a particle or a wave was dependent on the which-way data, and this outcome bolstered the beginning of quantum physics.

title: Addictions and Letting Go of Them
description: Addictions are hard to let go of when you only want to get rid of them at the intellectual level. The results tend to be temporary. If you want to get rid of an addiction at the being level, it will be much easier and more permanent.
videoTitle: Addictions and Letting Go of Them
captions: You know, those things feel good. We do them because we like to do them. And if we have to let those things go, and it's the same with the strawberry shortcake and all the, you know, the chocolate things, we do that because they taste good, because we like it. And we have comfort foods that make us feel better about ourselves. And to let that go is difficult. You really have to want to. And your intellect will want to, just until it stops wanting to, which won't take too long. Because it really, you don't want to give up the things you like. So it's a matter of your attachment to things, which is of course ego. And that attachment often comes out of fear for people. And that's why we have such a hard time keeping our promises to ourselves. Whether it's a New Year's resolution, or just one day you decide you need to lose weight. Because you look in the mirror and it's not a pretty sight, and you say, well, you know, that's not healthy. I should lose weight. And for the next two or three months, you probably, you know, are pretty good at it. But the point is, six months later, are you really still good at it? And a year or two years later, have you kind of gone back to the where you were in the first place? That's the difference between an intellectual commitment and a commitment at the being level. Commitment down at the root of who you really are. And if you get these commitments at the root of who you are, at that being level, then you will stick to them. Because it's not just something you're doing because you think you should. It's something you really want to do. It's something that's important to you to do. And then all the little things that get in the way, like I really like my strawberry shortcake, and I like my tea, and I like watching soap operas during the day. And for a month they try, and they do it pretty regularly, and then it gets regular and less regular to where they're kind of back where they were. So we tend to not make much progress because we're working from the intellect. That's not a very strong motivator. It only motivates us as long as we're focused on it. As soon as our focus slips, it slips away. That's kind of, I think, the key thing. And I have found that even if you have, you know, a physical addiction, say to nicotine, you know, you want to quit smoking. Of all the smokers in the world, probably at least half of them decide that they'd like to quit, you know, at least once a year or more, because it's an expensive habit, and mostly people around you don't like it, and it makes you go outside when it's cold. But now it's kind of a negative social thing. But people keep doing it anyway. They keep saying, well, yeah, I should quit. And they may quit for a few months, but they tend to come back to it because, again, it's intellectual. If it's a being level decision, I no longer want to be addicted, you know, to nicotine. I no longer want to be a drug addict where I have to do this thing. Otherwise, I get nervous or feel bad or whatever. I want to quit. When you really want to do it, the withdrawals disappear. It's when your intellect says you should do it, but you don't really want to at a deep-down level. It's just your intellect trying to push you. Now your withdrawals are terrible. You see other people smoking and you want to smoke. You get that cup of coffee after the meal and you want to smoke, you know, a cigarette with that cup of coffee and the withdrawals just nag at you and nag at you. title: Is it better to be open-minded or skeptical

videoTitle: Is it Better to be Open Minded or Skeptical?

title: Letting Go of Controlling Others

title: What Happens When We Die
description: Tom is asked what happens after we die? So he details the whole death process including the transition virtual reality, what happens to the avatar, the free will awareness units, and the individuated unit of consciousness
videoTitle: What Happens When We Die
captions: All right, now let me go through the whole process of what happens when you die, and we'll cover those things in it. When you die, you become aware in another virtual reality. So your body dies and you wake up, sort of like a, you know, we're no longer in Kansas. You know, you're in a different place. And in order, that is called the transition reality, and it's another virtual reality. You tend to have a little anxiety at that point, particularly if you come with fear, like, oh, is this hell or is this heaven? So there's some anxiety with it, or maybe it was a traumatic accident that you weren't planning to die, it just suddenly overcame you. But in any case, you will run into something, some, there'll be some strategy there to help you relax and let go of your past life. So it could be the light at the end of the tunnel, you know, all the things that the people who have the near-death experiences do, that's kind of the beginning of this pathway. Often there's the light and you get this intuition, that would be the larger conscious system sending you a message, move toward the light. So you do, and then as you do, you know, you find, you know, Aunt Susie and Uncle Fred, you know, there to greet you, because they passed on 10 years earlier, and they're smiling and they're happy and they're obviously having a good time, so it couldn't be too bad there. So these things are done just to put you at ease, make you feel relaxed, and let go. Your previous life begins to fade immediately, just like dreams do. You wake up from a dream, the instant you wake up, it's perfectly clear, 30 seconds later, it's a little fuzzy, a minute later, it's a lot fuzzy, and five minutes later, what was that dream about? I only remember a couple of major things, but all the detail disappears. So that's the way your memory of the last life just begins to fade like a dream. Now for the average person who has very little or no knowledge about the larger system, they go through a process that is basically designed to give them a chance to decompress and let go. So they're told to do non-functional things because you're just buying them time to decompress. Oh yes, welcome, you're here, Uncle Fred and Aunt Sally, they tell you and then they say, well, we're busy, we need to go, we'll see you a little bit later, and they take off. That's the larger conscious system, plain Uncle Fred and Aunt Sally, okay? So then they'll say, let's see, what's your name? Okay, over here, and there'll be a line of 15 people there, and you go stand in the line, and that takes a while. And if you finally do make it all the way up to the line, then they tell you a little something, or they tell you to go someplace else. And all it is is just keeping you from getting into a fit of uncertainty, giving you things to do. Meanwhile, the old reality is disappearing, disappearing, gone, all the people are nice, and everything seems to be friendly. You're not hungry or cold or wet, and it's all okay. And then eventually, you kind of feel like, well, what should I do next? What's going on? Kind of, what's happening here? And somebody will come approach you, and you will pretty soon, you'll be planning your next incarnation, where you're gonna go back and what it is you need to do. If you're just new in the business of being a consciousness and going into a virtual reality, if you're new at the business, it's a jump in, jump out. There's not a lot of planning. And just go back in, and you grab a body, and you have another experience, because what you need is experience, not a particular experience. If you've been around that block enough times that this part of you is developed, but this part, not so much. You wanna work on that part. So now you pick a certain kind of experience that you wanna go back into that has the probability of helping you develop that part that's weak. You may even have people that you go back with, because you really bring good stuff out in each other. You work well as a team. So now you may be incarnating with other people you've incarnated with before. If you've been around a whole lot more than that, you may go back almost with a scripted thing. You're going to do these things. You're going to help these people in this way, and you have a mission when you get here. So it goes from no scripting at all, jump in, jump out, to reasonably scripted, and everything in between. Okay, so that's what's going on. So then you decide to go. Now what actually has happened here is that when you die, that avatar, okay, the avatar that you were, Joe Jones, Joe Jones' avatar is dead. Joe Jones' the consciousness is not dead. The avatar is dead. Joe Jones' the consciousness is alive in a new reality frame. That avatar is what we call a free will awareness unit. And where that came from is that you had this individuated unit of consciousness, piece of the larger conscious system. It took a piece of itself, a piece that has no memory, no intellect, just the quality. It's a piece that contains the quality of that individuated unit of consciousness. All the things they've learned, the fear they've gotten rid of and all, it's got that quality. It's that free will awareness unit then with only the quality that logs on for the next incarnation. That's why it starts with no memory, no intellectual part, but it starts with all the quality that it's earned before. So the quality's cumulative. Every time around, whatever quality you earn, you come back in at that level with that quality. All the quality you lose because you've de-evolved, you come back in with less the next time. So that's kind of the way it goes. So what about the avatar is what you asked. That avatar, as soon as the avatar dies, that free will awareness unit starts to reintegrate with the individuated unit of consciousness. So think of it as a partition. You know how we partition hard drives? We take this much of the space and we say only these things go on in here and this other space is separate with different rules that apply to it. That's the way it is. So you have an IUOC and it puts a partition and that's the free will awareness unit, not in the intellectual part. When that avatar dies, that partition gets taken down. The partition gets taken down and now as that person is standing in line and just kind of working through the process of forgetting and becoming bored, that person now is no longer any representative of that avatar. It's now representative of the individuated unit of consciousness. Petitions down, that free will awareness unit is reintegrated. All right, that individuated unit of consciousness takes all the lifetimes, the last one along with all the rest of them and looks at them as a whole and says, what can I learn from all the lessons I've had? Because looking at the whole is more powerful than just looking at one individual one. So it looks through the whole set and then when it does, it says, well, I'm kind of weak over here. That's when that individual gets his talk and he says, well, you're a little weak over here. He's talking about the IUOC now, not the avatar. So then they plan for something else. So that avatar basically just gets reabsorbed into the individuated unit of consciousness that it was to begin with. Doesn't exist anymore, it's gone. But all the information that defined that particular avatar is still there in this collection of lifetimes. So everything that that avatar was, did, said, thought, felt, whatever, it's all collected here in this collection of lifetimes, experience packets. So it's still there. And that's what defines dead Uncle Fred when the medium comes in and calls him up because Aunt Susie has never been quite the same since his passing and she has some issues she needs to get rid of. That database that defines Uncle Fred precisely is the constraints that the largest conscious system used then to interact with Aunt Susie. So that's the way that works. So the avatar itself just gets reabsorbed. It disappears, but all the history of it, all the data describing it is there forever. When you go back and look at past lives, you're going back looking in a database. You're not going back and looking at beings that have free will and are still making choices. That's done. Now you're looking at a database. But this database is so complete that you can interact with it. You can talk to it. You can go back and change things. The database is laid out in terms of probability. So your Uncle Fred may have done any number of things given a stimulus. He's most likely to have done this, second most likely to have done that, third most likely to have done this. So you can go into these databases and like you're in, not seeing a movie, but you're in the movie. You can actually go into them and do what if analysis, change something. All right, Uncle Fred is gonna change something. What would have happened if I'd have married Sally instead of Susie? Well, he can go back and look at all the probabilities of where that would have taken him. It's just probable. Didn't actually happen. But you can go through that process. All that information's in the database of how Susie now would have interacted and he would have interacted with those interactions. Just in probability. So that's the kind of database it is. So the avatar itself, Joe Jones, is absorbed into its IUOC, Individuated Unit of Consciousness. And it basically is no more as far as a free will operating consciousness. But all his data's there in this Individuated Units of Consciousness of which he originated.

title: Getting Angry is a Choice
description: Anger comes from insecurity, of judging people and things, wishing them to be different from how they are.
videoTitle: Getting Angry is a Choice
captions: What we know and understand, we understand what would be good for everybody. We know how everybody should be. We know how our children should be. We know how our husbands and wives should be. We know how our in-laws and our parents, we know how everybody in the world should be. And we are certain that if they would just be the way we want them to be, everything would be terrific. But of course, everybody feels that way. Every individual feels that they know what would be best for everyone else. And they don't realize that each of them are in their own reality, living their own life in their own way. And this, they have emotions, they have feelings, they get upset, they get angry. But that anger is a choice. They choose to be angry. And they'll point their finger at somebody else and say, you make me angry. But nobody can make you angry. You choose to be angry. And you get angry because of a fear that you have, because somebody said something that triggers one of your fears. And your response to that is to get angry, you see. So yes, we all live in our own reality. We all have our own emotions. And we all believe that we know what's best for everybody else. And of course, that just doesn't work. It's so much better if you realize that other people just are who they are. Let them be how they are. Don't wish them to be different. Don't want to change them. Don't try to change them. Learn how to be positive with them just the way they are. And if there's negatives in there, well, let those go. They're not that important. Ignore the negatives and just interact with the positives. Don't push their buttons. Avoid their buttons. Don't set them off by saying things that you know are going to be upsetting to them. And in that way, you can have a good positive relationship with almost anybody, even people that now you don't like so much, people at the office you don't really get along with. You can have good relationship with them if you just let them be and stop judging them according to what you think, how you think they should be. They shouldn't be like that. They shouldn't say things like that. They shouldn't have that attitude. And now we get upset about what they should and shouldn't have. That's us judging them according to our reality and the way we feel. And of course, they are probably judging us, you know, according to what their reality is. And they just have a lot of people all fussing and fighting and fuming with each other all the time because they just don't understand reality and how it works and that we're all different. We need to just accept that. Let people be different. Everybody is doing the best they can with what they've got to work with. And what they've got to work with is a lot of beliefs and fears and things that they learned in childhood and adulthood. And that's what makes them the way they are. That's what makes them insecure. Well, when you're insecure, you can express that in two ways. You can express it in being a shrinking violet that just doesn't say much and shrinks off to the side. But that's not the way most people express it. When you're insecure, most people express it by being belligerent, by being tough, by being, this is my way, my way or the highway. And you become arrogant and forceful, and other people need to do it your way because your way is right. That's the way people hide their feelings of being insecure, by being blustery. It denies the insecurity. So that's kind of the way most people deal with it. And of course, that's just very, it's just the thing that will annoy and bother somebody else who also is self-centered because what you're doing and your feelings are just not the way they see the world. So yes, let people be. Let them be who they are and don't impose your view of the world on everybody else. Just make sure that the things that you do are good things, are low-entropy things, which means you don't get angry because everything negative is a low-entropy bad thing. Once you get rid of your fear, you no longer get angry. You no longer get upset. You no longer feel used and abused and unsatisfied and not treated well. All of that stuff just disappears when your fears disappear. You see things differently and you take responsibility for yourself. If you start to get angry, you realize that's you, not them. You are getting angry because they are triggering one of your fears. You need to get rid of that fear. You need to not be triggered like that. You need to let them be the way they are and make it so you're impossible to trigger. Nothing can trigger you. If somebody's rude to you, you think, gee, they must really be having a hard day because they must be feeling really miserable for them to be kind of rude like that. See, I wonder if there's anything I could say to help them out. Instead of getting angry, you feel compassion for people who are rude to you because you know they're having a hard time and they're upset. Their ego and their fear is giving them a hard time. You either just get out of the way or you see if you can be helpful. But you don't start fussing at them because that's just throwing gasoline on a fire that's already burning and it just makes everything worse.

title: The Inevitable Paradigm Shift
description: Tom Campbell predicts that a paradigm shift in our understanding of reality is inevitable, driven by the discoveries of modern physics, particularly quantum mechanics. He explains that as science increasingly points to an information-based, computed reality, the belief in a purely material world will become untenable.  Tom delves into how the cultural belief in a material reality shapes our societal ethics and individual behaviors. He explains that this belief naturally leads to a focus on competition for physical resources, fostering a self-centered, control-based ethic. This, in turn, influences everything from our economic systems to our personal goals, such as the pursuit of money and power. He contrasts this with an understanding of a consciousness-based reality, which would fundamentally alter our values and priorities.
videoTitle: What Will Shift Our Reality From Fear to Love?

title: The Role of Science in Shifting Paradigms
description: Tom discusses the pivotal role of science in initiating a global shift in understanding reality. He suggests that as physics continues to uncover the information-based nature of our universe, it will provide the logical foundation for people to question and ultimately abandon the materialist belief system. This scientific validation, he argues, will be the catalyst for a broader cultural and spiritual evolution.  Tom predicts that the transition to a new paradigm will be a gradual but potentially turbulent process, taking several decades. He likens this shift to a snowball effect, where the initial change in perspective will gain momentum and lead to widespread transformation. He acknowledges the difficulty of this change, especially for a culture deeply entrenched in materialism, but remains optimistic about humanity's ability to navigate it.
videoTitle: What Will Shift Our Reality From Fear to Love?

title: Future Outlook
